input.question: How do the same programs run on different operating systems?
input.ground_truth: There are development languages that are cross platform. This is one way this can be accomplished. The same code base will run in various environments (Linux/BSD/Windows) and then OS specific code can be ran inside the software that is called based on what environment the code detects. Also, a second way would be runtime emulation such as WINE, but I don't think that is what you are referring to

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How do the same programs run on different operating systems?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy car. You can play with your toy car on the floor at home, or you can take it to the park or even to grandma’s house. The toy car is the same, but the places you play with it are different.

Now, think of a computer program as a toy car, and the operating system as the floor where you play. Different operating systems (like Windows, Mac, or Linux) are like different kinds of floors. 

Some special toy cars (programs) are made in a way that they can roll and play on any kind of floor. These are called "cross-platform" programs. They are built so they can work on many different operating systems.

Other toy cars (programs) are only made to work on one kind of floor. Those are called "platform-specific" programs.

So, the same program can run on different operating systems if it is made to be friendly with all of them, just like how some toy cars can play on any floor!
